body.cap: AramHuvis presented AI-Scalp Grader (AISG) and won CES 2023 Innovation Award. │Photo by Aving News

body.x: [Las Vegas, U.S. = Aving News] AramHuvis (CEO Dongsoon Park) announced that they participated in CES 2023 held in Las Vegas, U.S. for four days from Thursday, January 5 to Sunday, January 8, 2023 in local time.

Founded in November 2002, AramHuvis has been manufacturing and distributing cosmetic diagnostic devices for skin, scalp, and hair for over 20 years. The experience and knowledge gained while growing with global beauty businesses is now the foundation for customized cosmetics business it pursues. Starting from the partnerships with South Korea's leading hair salon franchises, the company is planning to expand its market while getting ready to build a system that enables everyone in the world to use their unique suitable hair products.
The company aims at providing custom-made solution products to the end consumers, taking advantage of this exhibition as an opportunity to establish a network.

AI-Scalp Grader (AISG) presented at CES 2023 is an AI scalp diagnostic device trained with AramHuvis' exclusive big data and analytical technology. All those seeking scalp care can be provided with custom-made ingredients subdivided into 1 mg depending on their scalp type.

According to an AramHuvis representative, “We have trained artificial intelligence with over 100,000 pieces of biometric data collected with our diagnostic devices over the past 20 years. That led to the development of AISG, a smart system that offers detailed and accurate diagnostic reports based on a picture of the scalp. For business owners in the beauty industry, our products are a very effective way to promote services and attract consumers. AISG also allows average users to get accurate data on their scalp conditions.”

body.cap: Scalp Diagnosis Demonstration │Photo by Aving News

body.x: AramHuvis’ hair products created with this AISG technology are made with active ingredients tailored to the individual scalp type. “Solutions to scalp-related problems (dryness, oiliness, sensitivity, seborrhoea, etc.) and their distribution systems were hard to find globally. In contrast, the scalp and hair loss management market is continuously expanding, and issues such as scalp disease and hair loss are also increasingly emerging in younger generation who are socially active in particular. As the demand for individual management based on accurate diagnostic information is expected to increase, we wanted to secure future-readiness and profitability by combining a scalp care system and a solution product,” said the representative.

The representative further explained that “We expect to contribute to the enhancement of the user's standard of living with our scalp diagnostics and custom-made scalp product manufacturing processes using our AI algorithm.”

AramHuvis also reported its achievements from the participation in CES. With the help of its partner Estee Lauder, they succeeded in introducing the system to two U.S. branches who are currently running a pilot project, which is before the stage where practical sales performance can be discussed with display and system.

“There have been a lot of inquiries from end consumers interested in scalp care products as well as business owners who run beauty-related businesses or care products sales businesses from home and abroad, hoping to adopt the diagnostic system quickly.” “As we expect to attract a large number of customers who use AI-Scalp Grader, the demand for convenient diagnostic devices will rise. That is why we developed a small handheld model ECW-CUBE, which is ready for launch. As soon as the sales of AISG are stabilized, it will be distributed as a pilot project in the stores,” the representative explained.

body.cap: Photo of AramHubis’ booth at CES 2023 │Photo by Aving News

body.x: “When representatives of our longtime partners and global beauty companies, LOREAL, P&G, and Estee Laude, visited our booth, we had presentations on our products and completed a survey on the adoption of AISG by country. This is an essential foundation for future supply of AISG and custom-made scalp cosmetics. Meaningful discussions have been made beyond our prior expectations,” the representative said.

Meanwhile, AramHuvis services are based on big data and artificial intelligence (AI) technology. AI learning requires a large amount of data, and a variety of data to accumulate. In addition to the data collected on its own, AramHuvis was able to reinforce the performance of their existing AI models by utilizing the open AI learning data through AI-Hub established by the Ministry of Science and ICT and the National Information Society Agency.

Organized by the Ministry of Science and ICT and promoted by the National Information Society Agency, the data building project for AI learning which has built a total of 1,300 types of data will remain open to the public via AI-Hub until 2025. This project has addressed the difficulty in cost-and-time-consuming data building, driving growth of AI SMEs and startups in Korea. The data for AI learning can be accessed and downloaded by the public on the AI-Hub website.
